findings.title: Target OU Retail is registered with Control Tower; the account has to be enrolled
findings.detail: Moving into a registered OU does not enroll the account by itself. The 3 preventive guardrail SCP(s) on the OU chain apply immediately because they are attached to the OUs, but the 4 detective control(s) do not report and the baseline is not deployed until the account is enrolled from Account Factory. Enrolment needs an AWSControlTowerExecution role in the account that trusts management account 222222222221, no conflicting Config recorder or delivery channel in the governed regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), and an email address and name that Account Factory can register. The account has to have joined o-fernhill0001 before it can be enrolled.

checks.summary: 3 assignment(s) across 3 permission set(s) and 3 provisioned role(s) go away with the move; 2 permission set name(s) exist in the target, 1 do not.

findings.title: 3 AWSReservedSSO_* role(s) are deleted from the account: AWSReservedSSO_AdministratorAccess_*, AWSReservedSSO_ReadOnlyAccess_*, AWSReservedSSO_DataPlatformOperator_*
findings.detail: Identity Center deletes the IAM roles it provisioned in the account (path /aws-reserved/sso.amazonaws.com/us-east-1/) when the account leaves the organization. Anything that names these roles breaks: resource and trust policies, KMS key policies, S3 bucket policies, EKS access entries, pipelines and tools that assume them, and CloudTrail history keeps the old ARNs. The target instance provisions new roles with a different random suffix, so references have to be updated, not restored. The exact suffix is only visible in IAM; offline the roles are known by their pattern.
